# report/report.md and SARIF `help`. "TBD" where remediation is genuinely context-specific.

column2: Restrict Spring Boot Actuator endpoints: expose only /health, bind management to an internal port, and require authentication (management.endpoints.web.exposure.include, Spring Security).
Do not serve Swagger/OpenAPI/GraphQL schema publicly in production; gate behind auth or disable, and treat any leaked endpoints as attack surface to review.
Enforce function-level authorization server-side on every privileged action (deny-by-default); never rely on UI hiding. Verify role on the endpoint, not the client.
Normalise/deny caching of authenticated responses; make the cache key include auth state; reject path-confusion (e.g. /account/foo.css) at the origin.
Include every request input that affects the response in the cache key, or strip unkeyed inputs (X-Forwarded-Host, etc.) before caching.
Send Content-Security-Policy: frame-ancestors 'self' (or specific origins) and X-Frame-Options on all sensitive pages.
Make buckets private by default; block public ACLs/policies; enable public-access-block; audit with least-privilege IAM.
Never pass user input to a shell; use parameterised APIs (execFile with an arg array), strict allow-lists, and drop shell metacharacters.
Remove exposed config/backup/.env files from web roots; deny dotfiles and backups at the server; rotate any leaked secrets.
Do not reflect arbitrary Origin with credentials; use a strict allow-list of origins and never combine Access-Control-Allow-Origin:* with credentials.
Reject/encode CR and LF in any value written to response headers; use framework header APIs that forbid injection.
Change all default/admin credentials, enforce a strong-password policy, and disable or firewall default management interfaces.
Do not deserialise untrusted data; use data-only formats (JSON) with schemas; if unavoidable, enforce allow-listed types and integrity (signed payloads).
Disable directory listing (Options -Indexes / autoindex off) and return 404 for directories without an index.
Remove dangling NS/CNAME records pointing to unclaimed providers; monitor DNS for stale delegations.
Restrict admin/login panels to trusted networks or VPN, add authentication + rate limiting, and avoid predictable paths.
Validate type by content (not extension), store outside the web root, randomise names, disable execution in the upload dir, and scan uploads.
Disable introspection in production, enforce field-level authorization, add query depth/complexity limits and rate limiting.
Validate the Host header against an allow-list; do not build absolute URLs (password-reset links, cache keys) from the untrusted Host.
Enforce object-level authorization on every access (the resource must belong to the caller); use unguessable references and check ownership server-side.
Pin the algorithm server-side (reject 'none' and alg confusion), verify signature with a strong key, validate exp/aud/iss, and rotate keys.
Patch/upgrade the affected component to a fixed version; where patching lags, apply the vendor mitigation and virtual patching at the WAF.
Enforce business invariants server-side (state transitions, quantities, ownership); add idempotency and server-side validation of every step.
Bind only an explicit allow-list of fields to models; never auto-bind request bodies to privileged attributes (role, isAdmin, price).
Use parameterised queries/typed schemas; reject query operators in user input; validate types (a string is not an object).
Strictly validate redirect_uri against an exact allow-list, use state/PKCE, bind tokens to the client, and never expose tokens via open redirects.
Use an allow-list of redirect targets or relative paths only; never redirect to a user-supplied absolute URL.
Use single-use, expiring, high-entropy tokens bound to the account; do not leak tokens; validate the reset belongs to the requesting user; don't build links from the Host header.
Canonicalise and confine paths to a base directory (reject ../ and encodings); prefer opaque IDs over filesystem paths; least-privilege file access.
Reject __proto__/constructor/prototype keys in user input; use Map or Object.create(null); freeze prototypes; update vulnerable libraries.
Use atomic operations / row locks / idempotency keys for state-changing actions; do not check-then-act without a transaction.
Normalise/deny ambiguous Content-Length vs Transfer-Encoding; use HTTP/2 end-to-end or a front-end that rejects conflicting framing.
Verify the SAML signature over the full assertion, reject unsigned/wrapped assertions (XSW), validate audience/recipient/conditions, and pin the IdP cert.
Rotate the leaked secret immediately, remove it from client/JS bundles, move secrets server-side, and add secret scanning to CI.
Use secure, HttpOnly, SameSite cookies; regenerate the session id on login; expire and invalidate on logout; bind sessions to context.
Remove exposed .git/.svn/source maps/backups from production; deny them at the server; rotate any secrets found in recovered source.
Use parameterised queries / prepared statements everywhere; never concatenate input into SQL; apply least-privilege DB accounts.
Enforce an egress allow-list, resolve-and-pin destinations, block link-local/metadata ranges, disable unused URL schemes, and enforce IMDSv2.
Never render user input as a template; pass user data as template variables, not template source; sandbox the engine and update it.
Remove dangling CNAMEs to unclaimed services or reclaim the resource; monitor DNS for stale third-party pointers.
Validate the Origin on the WebSocket handshake, authenticate/authorize per message, and do not trust cross-origin connections (CSWSH).
Contextual output encoding for every sink, a strict Content-Security-Policy, HttpOnly cookies, and framework auto-escaping; sanitise HTML with a vetted library.
Disable external entities and DTD processing in the XML parser (FEATURE_SECURE_PROCESSING / disallow-doctype-decl); prefer non-XML formats.
